name: ristretto-67cb5913-blind29-ots
instr:
# Diagnosing 29 injected one-line faults in ristretto without a test suite

I use this library to keep a bounded set of key-and-value pairs in memory, and I lean on the low-level helpers it comes with too: raw byte regions, semicolon-separated option text, percentile measurements, an on-disk sorted key-and-value structure and access-trace files. Nothing in my own code changed, yet a great many ordinary uses now answer wrongly. The repository has received 29 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything I could pin down from the outside, arranged by what I was doing at the time.

The worst of it is that the second, collision-guarding number I pass alongside a key is no longer honoured when I read an entry or when I take one out. I put a value in under a key with that number as zero, then looked the key up passing one: instead of the miss I expected, the lookup succeeded and handed me the value back. Asking for that same key to be taken out while passing a number that disagrees with the entry actually held removes the entry anyway, so an entry the mismatch should have protected is gone afterwards. Lookups that pass zero, meaning do not check, behave as they always did, and revising a value through a mismatched number is still refused.

Turning an ordinary integer key into the pair of numbers that identifies it inside yields the first of the pair exactly as before, in every signed, unsigned and sized width, but the second of the pair now comes back as one where it used
